paper.shortTitle: The Open Catalyst 2022 (OC22) Dataset and Challenges for Oxide
paper.authors: Richard Tran, Janice Lan, Muhammed Shuaibi et al.

nodes.title: Research question
nodes.body: How can the target scientific task be compared under fixed data and evaluation rules?

nodes.title: Freeze tasks and metrics
nodes.body: To address this, we developed the OC22 dataset, consisting of 62,331 DFT relaxations (~9,854,504 single point calculations) across a range of oxide materials, coverages, and adsorbates.

nodes.title: Evaluate reference systems
nodes.body: In the most general task, GemNet-OC sees a ~36% improvement in energy predictions when combining the chemically dissimilar OC20 and OC22 datasets via fine-tuning.

nodes.title: Primary reported result
nodes.body: We define generalized total energy tasks that enable property prediction beyond adsorption energies; we test baseline performance of several graph neural networks; and we provide pre-defined dataset splits to establish clear benchmarks for future efforts.

nodes.title: Published conclusion
nodes.body: Dataset and baseline models are open sourced, and a public leaderboard is available to encourage continued community developments on the total energy tasks and data.
